_about: Blessed and sent (plan 7.6b): blessings spoken and charges given, each set beside the places that repeat or take up its words, from Genesis to Acts and Revelation, with what is alike and what differs. Every quotation machine-checked against the Berean; rows chosen and drafted by Claude Opus from the passages the theme map cites and a search of the whole Berean; widened by the completeness search; every Alike and Different line read by the nine-reader panel (Sonnet). Takes no interpretive stance. A cell [verse, words, "aside"] is off the subject and shown, with an asterisk, for its shared words.
columns_note: The Prophets: Isaiah to Malachi. Psalms & elsewhere: any other Old Testament book.

rows.title: Be fruitful and multiply

Genesis: Be fruitful and multiply and fill the waters of the seas
Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth
be fruitful and multiply upon it
Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth
be fruitful and multiply; spread out across the earth and multiply upon it
I will make you exceedingly fruitful
I will make him fruitful and multiply him greatly
May God Almighty bless you and make you fruitful and multiply you
became fruitful and increased greatly in number
I will make you fruitful and multiply you
The Prophets: where they will be fruitful and multiply
I will fill you with people and animals, and they will multiply and be fruitful
Psalms & elsewhere: the Israelites were fruitful and increased rapidly; they multiplied
make you fruitful and multiply you

rows.alike: All but Genesis 17:6 join 'fruitful' to 'multiply' (in Genesis 47:27, to 'increased greatly in number'); Genesis 17:6 has 'exceedingly fruitful' alone. God says 'Be fruitful and multiply' to the creatures of the seas and the birds (Genesis 1:22), to the man and woman (1:28), to Noah and his sons (9:1, 9:7) and to Jacob (35:11).
rows.different: Genesis 1:22, 1:28, 9:1 and 35:11 give it as a command; Genesis 17:6, 48:4 and Leviticus 26:9 have God say 'I will make you fruitful'; Genesis 28:3 is a wish, 'May God Almighty bless you and make you fruitful and multiply you'. Genesis 47:27 and Exodus 1:7 report it of the Israelites in Egypt; Jeremiah 23:3 says it of the remnant gathered back, and Ezekiel 36:11 has the order reversed, 'multiply and be fruitful'.

rows.title: Fill the earth

Genesis: fill the waters of the seas
fill the earth and subdue it
Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth
The Prophets: the earth will be full of the knowledge of the LORD as the sea is full of water
Israel will bud and blossom and fill the whole world with fruit
the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the LORD as the waters cover the sea
Psalms & elsewhere: so that the land was filled with them
the whole earth is filled with the glory of the LORD
may all the earth be filled with His glory

rows.alike: Genesis 1:28 and 9:1 both say 'fill the earth' to those God has just blessed, and Exodus 1:7 reports of the Israelites that 'the land was filled with them'.
rows.different: Genesis 1:22 says 'fill the waters of the seas' to the sea creatures, and Exodus 1:7 has 'the land', not 'the earth'. In the asides the earth is filled with something else: 'the glory of the LORD' (Numbers 14:21), 'His glory' (Psalm 72:19), 'the knowledge of the LORD' (Isaiah 11:9), 'the knowledge of the glory of the LORD' (Habakkuk 2:14), and in Isaiah 27:6 Israel will 'fill the whole world with fruit'.

rows.title: Rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of the air

Genesis: to rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of the air
fill the earth and subdue it; rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of the air
The fear and dread of you will fall on every living creature on the earth, every bird of the air
all the fish of the sea. They are delivered into your hand
The man gave names to all the livestock, to the birds of the air, and to every beast of the field
The Prophets: He has given them into your hand and has made you ruler over them all
You are that head of gold
the birds of the air; even the fish of the sea disappear
I will sweep away the birds of the air, and the fish of the sea
The fish of the sea, the birds of the air, the beasts of the field, every creature that crawls upon the ground
Psalms & elsewhere: You made him ruler of the works of Your hands; You have placed everything under his feet
the birds of the air and the fish of the sea
the earth He has given to mankind
all sheep and oxen, and even the beasts of the field
ask the birds of the air, and they will tell you
let the fish of the sea inform you
put his enemies under his feet
bird that flies in the air
any creature that crawls on the ground or fish that is in the waters below
The letters: God has put everything under His feet
this clearly does not include the One who put everything under Him
and placed everything under his feet
Yet at present we do not see everything subject to him
put all His enemies under His feet
God put everything under His feet and made Him head over everything for the church
All kinds of animals, birds, reptiles, and creatures of the sea are being tamed and have been tamed by man
images of mortal man and birds and animals and reptiles

rows.alike: Genesis 1:26, 1:28 and Psalm 8:6-8 name the same creatures, 'the fish of the sea and the birds of the air', under a rule God gives: 'rule over' in Genesis, 'You made him ruler' in the psalm. Psalm 8:7 goes on "all sheep and oxen, and even the beasts of the field".
rows.different: Genesis 1:28 has 'subdue it' where 1:26 does not; Genesis 9:2 has 'The fear and dread of you will fall' on them and 'They are delivered into your hand'. Hebrews 2:8 has 'placed everything under his feet' and adds 'Yet at present we do not see everything subject to him'; 1 Corinthians 15:27 has 'God has put everything under His feet' and adds that 'this clearly does not include the One who put everything under Him', and 1 Corinthians 15:25 says of 'all His enemies' that He 'must reign until' they are under His feet. Ephesians 1:22 has 'God put everything under His feet' and adds 'made Him head over everything for the church'. In Daniel 2:38 'ruler over them all' is said to one who is told 'You are that head of gold'. Genesis 2:20 has the man give "names to all the livestock, to the birds of the air, and to every beast of the field"; James 3:7 says "All kinds of animals, birds, reptiles, and creatures of the sea are being tamed and have been tamed by man". The same creatures are named elsewhere of other things: Job 12:7-8 says "ask the birds of the air" and "let the fish of the sea inform you"; Hosea says the "fish of the sea disappear", Zephaniah has them swept away, and Ezekiel has them "tremble at My presence"; Deuteronomy 4:17-18 has "bird that flies in the air" and "fish that is in the waters below", and Romans names birds among the "images" for which the glory of God was exchanged; and 1 Kings 5:3 says the LORD "had put his enemies under his feet" of David.

rows.title: Leave your country and go to the land I will show you

Genesis: Leave your country, your kindred, and your father's household, and go to the land I will show you
So Abram departed, as the LORD had directed him
Psalms & elsewhere: Leave this place, you and the people you brought up out of the land of Egypt, and go to the land that I promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob
Gospels & Acts: Leave your country and your kindred and go to the land I will show you
The letters: By faith Abraham, when called to go to a place he would later receive as his inheritance, obeyed and went, without knowing where he was going

rows.alike: Genesis 12:1 and Acts 7:3 give the charge to Abram in nearly the same words, 'go to the land I will show you', and Genesis 12:4 and Hebrews 11:8 both record that he went: 'So Abram departed', 'obeyed and went'.
rows.different: Acts 7:3 leaves out 'your father's household'. Hebrews 11:8 says he went 'By faith' and 'without knowing where he was going'. In Exodus 33:1 the charge 'Leave this place ... and go to the land' is given to Moses and the people, to 'the land that I promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob'.

rows.title: I will make you into a great nation

Genesis: I will make you into a great nation
I will make him into a great nation
Abraham will surely become a great and powerful nation
for I will make him into a great nation
Do not be afraid to go down to Egypt, for I will make you into a great nation there
Psalms & elsewhere: so that My anger may burn against them and consume them. Then I will make you into a great nation
I will strike them with a plague and destroy them-and I will make you into a nation greater and mightier than they are
went down to Egypt few in number and lived there and became a great nation, mighty and numerous
Then I will make you into a nation mightier and greater than they are
Gospels & Acts: He made them into a great people during their stay in Egypt

rows.alike: God says 'I will make you into a great nation' to Abram (Genesis 12:2), to Jacob (46:3) and to Moses (Exodus 32:10), and 'I will make him into a great nation' of Ishmael (Genesis 17:20, 21:18); to Moses again, 'I will make you into a nation mightier and greater than they are' (Deuteronomy 9:14).
rows.different: Genesis 46:3 adds 'there', in Egypt, and Deuteronomy 26:5 has Israel declare that its father 'became a great nation, mighty and numerous' there; Acts 13:17 says 'He made them into a great people during their stay in Egypt'. To Moses it follows 'consume them' (Exodus 32:10) and 'destroy them' (Numbers 14:12), and Numbers has 'a nation greater and mightier than they are'.

rows.title: I will surely bless you and multiply you

Genesis: By Myself I have sworn, declares the LORD
I will surely bless you, and I will multiply your descendants
I will be with you and bless you
I will bless you and multiply your descendants for the sake of My servant Abraham
I will surely bless him; I will make him fruitful and multiply him greatly
The Prophets: But from this day on, I will bless you
Psalms & elsewhere: He will love you and bless you and multiply you
Gospels & Acts: He sent Him first to you to bless you by turning each of you from your wicked ways
The letters: I will surely bless you and multiply your descendants

rows.alike: God says 'I will bless you' to Abram (Genesis 12:2), Abraham (22:17) and Isaac (26:3, 26:24), and Hebrews 6:14 gives the words to Abraham as 'I will surely bless you and multiply your descendants'.
rows.different: Genesis 22:16 and Hebrews 6:13 both frame it as an oath: 'By Myself I have sworn', 'He swore by Himself'. Genesis 26:24 adds 'for the sake of My servant Abraham'; Genesis 17:20 says it of Ishmael, 'I will make him fruitful and multiply him greatly'; Deuteronomy 7:13 says it to the people, 'He will love you and bless you and multiply you'; Haggai 2:19 dates it, 'from this day on'; Acts 3:26 says God sent His Servant 'to bless you by turning each of you from your wicked ways'.

rows.title: I will make your name great

Genesis: I will make your name great
that we may make a name for ourselves
Psalms & elsewhere: I have been with you wherever you have gone
Now I will make for you a name like that of the greatest in the land
Now I will make for you a name like that of the greatest in the land

rows.alike: God promises a name to Abram, 'I will make your name great' (Genesis 12:2), and to David, 'I will make for you a name like that of the greatest in the land' (2 Samuel 7:9, 1 Chronicles 17:8).
rows.different: To David the promise follows 'I have been with you wherever you have gone'. In Genesis 11:4 it is the builders of the city who say 'that we may make a name for ourselves'.

rows.title: You will be a blessing

Genesis: so that you will be a blessing
The Prophets: Israel will join a three-party alliance with Egypt and Assyria-a blessing upon the earth
Blessed be Egypt My people, Assyria My handiwork, and Israel My inheritance
I will make them and the places around My hill a blessing
As you have been a curse among the nations, O house of Judah and house of Israel, so I will save you, and you will be a blessing

rows.alike: Genesis 12:2 and Zechariah 8:13 both have 'you will be a blessing', and Isaiah 19:24 and Ezekiel 34:26 also use 'a blessing' of those they name.
rows.different: Genesis 12:2 is said to Abram; Zechariah 8:13 to the 'house of Judah and house of Israel', who 'have been a curse among the nations'; Isaiah 19:24-25 joins Israel 'with Egypt and Assyria' as 'a blessing upon the earth', calling them 'Egypt My people, Assyria My handiwork, and Israel My inheritance'.

rows.title: Bless those who bless you, curse those who curse you

Genesis: I will bless those who bless you and curse those who curse you
May those who curse you be cursed, and those who bless you be blessed
Psalms & elsewhere: Blessed are those who bless you and cursed are those who curse you

rows.alike: All three bless those who bless, and curse those who curse, the one addressed.
rows.different: In Genesis 12:3 God speaks to Abram, 'I will bless'; in Genesis 27:29 Isaac blesses Jacob, 'May those who curse you be cursed', putting the curse first; in Numbers 24:9 Balaam says it of Israel, 'Blessed are those who bless you'.

rows.title: All the families of the earth will be blessed through you

Genesis: all the families of the earth will be blessed through you
through him all the nations of the earth will be blessed
through your offspring all nations of the earth will be blessed, because you have obeyed My voice
through your offspring all nations of the earth will be blessed
All the families of the earth will be blessed through you and your offspring
The Prophets: in truth, in justice, and in righteousness, then the nations will be blessed by Him
Only you have I known from all the families of the earth
Then all the nations will call you blessed
Psalms & elsewhere: In him may all nations be blessed; may they call him blessed
All the families of the nations will bow down before Him
Gospels & Acts: Through your offspring all the families of the earth will be blessed
The letters: All nations will be blessed through you
So those who have faith are blessed along with Abraham, the man of faith

rows.alike: Each says a blessing reaches everyone: 'all the families of the earth' (Genesis 12:3, 28:14, Acts 3:25), 'all the nations of the earth' (Genesis 18:18, 22:18, 26:4), 'all nations' (Psalm 72:17, Galatians 3:8).
rows.different: Genesis 12:3 says 'through you', 22:18 and 26:4 'through your offspring', and 28:14 'through you and your offspring'; Genesis 22:18 adds 'because you have obeyed My voice'. Psalm 72:17 is a prayer, 'May his name endure forever ... In him may all nations be blessed'; Jeremiah 4:2 makes it follow 'if you can swear' and says 'blessed by Him'. Galatians 3:8 gives 'All nations will be blessed through you' after 'God would justify the Gentiles by faith', and 3:9 adds 'those who have faith are blessed along with Abraham'.

rows.title: The blessing on you and your offspring

Genesis: may He give the blessing of Abraham to you and your descendants, so that you may possess the land where you dwell as a foreigner
The Prophets: I will pour out My Spirit on your descendants, and My blessing on your offspring
Their descendants will be known among the nations, and their offspring among the peoples
they are a people the LORD has blessed
they will be a people blessed by the LORD-they and their descendants with them
The letters: the blessing promised to Abraham would come to the Gentiles in Christ Jesus
The promises were spoken to Abraham and to his seed

rows.alike: Each speaks of a blessing given to someone and those who come after: 'the blessing of Abraham to you and your descendants' (Genesis 28:4), 'My blessing on your offspring' (Isaiah 44:3), 'a people blessed by the LORD-they and their descendants with them' (Isaiah 65:23), 'spoken to Abraham and to his seed' (Galatians 3:16).
rows.different: Genesis 28:4 is Isaac's prayer for Jacob and ties the blessing to possessing 'the land where you dwell as a foreigner'; Isaiah 44:3 sets it beside 'I will pour out My Spirit'. Galatians 3:14 says the blessing promised to Abraham 'would come to the Gentiles in Christ Jesus', and Galatians 3:16 reads 'and to your seed' as 'meaning One, who is Christ'.

rows.title: A father of many nations

Genesis: You will be the father of many nations
your name will be Abraham, for I have made you a father of many nations
she will be the mother of nations
so that you may become a company of peoples
A nation-even a company of nations-shall come from you
his offspring shall become a multitude of nations
The letters: I have made you a father of many nations
Against all hope, Abraham in hope believed and so became the father of many nations

rows.alike: Genesis 17:4-5 and Romans 4:17-18 share the words 'father of many nations', and Romans 4:17 quotes Genesis 17:5, 'I have made you a father of many nations'.
rows.different: Genesis 17:5 ties it to the new name, 'your name will be Abraham'; Romans 4:18 ties it to belief, 'Abraham in hope believed and so became the father of many nations'. Genesis 17:16 says of Sarah 'she will be the mother of nations', and 28:3, 35:11 and 48:19 have 'a company of peoples', 'a company of nations' and 'a multitude of nations'.

rows.title: As the stars of the sky and the sand on the seashore

Genesis: I will make your offspring like the dust of the earth
count the stars, if you are able
I will multiply your descendants like the stars in the sky and the sand on the seashore
I will make your descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky
Your descendants will be like the dust of the earth
I will make your offspring like the sand of the sea, too numerous to count
like the sand of the sea
The Prophets: Though your people, O Israel, be like the sand of the sea, only a remnant will return
Your descendants would have been as countless as the sand, and your offspring as numerous as its grains
as the sand on the seashore cannot be measured, so too will I multiply the descendants of My servant David and the Levites who minister before Me
the number of the Israelites will be like the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured or counted
Psalms & elsewhere: I will make your descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky
Who can count the dust of Jacob
today you are as numerous as the stars in the sky
now the LORD your God has made you as numerous as the stars in the sky
You who were as numerous as the stars in the sky will be left few in number, because you would not obey the voice of the LORD your God
all Israel from Dan to Beersheba-a multitude like the sand on the seashore
The people of Judah and Israel were as numerous as the sand on the seashore
the LORD had said that He would make Israel as numerous as the stars of the sky
a people as numerous as the dust of the earth
like the sand on the seashore
like the sand of the sea
The letters: Though the number of the Israelites is like the sand of the sea, only the remnant will be saved
And so from one man, and he as good as dead, came descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky and as countless as the sand on the seashore
Revelation: Their number is like the sand of the seashore

rows.alike: Each counts the descendants of Abraham, or Israel, by what cannot be counted: 'the stars in the sky', 'the sand on the seashore', 'the dust of the earth'.
rows.different: Genesis has 'I will make' and 'I will multiply'; Deuteronomy 1:10 says 'today you are as numerous as the stars in the sky' and 1 Kings 4:20 'The people of Judah and Israel were as numerous as the sand on the seashore'; Deuteronomy 28:62 says they 'will be left few in number, because you would not obey'. Isaiah 10:22 and Romans 9:27 add 'only a remnant will return', 'only the remnant will be saved'; Jeremiah 33:22 says it of 'the descendants of My servant David and the Levites'; Hebrews 11:12 says they came 'from one man, and he as good as dead'. Revelation 20:8 uses the words of the nations gathered as 'Gog and Magog'. Genesis 41:49, 1 Kings 4:29 and Psalm 78:27 use 'like the sand' of Joseph's grain, of Solomon's understanding and of birds, not of descendants.

rows.title: I will give this land to your offspring

Genesis: I will give this land to your offspring
all the land that you see, I will give to you and your offspring forever
to you and your descendants I will give the land where you are residing-all the land of Canaan-as an eternal possession
For I will give all these lands to you and your offspring

will give this land to your descendants after you as an everlasting possession
Psalms & elsewhere: I will give your descendants all this land that I have promised
I will give it to your descendants
This is the land that I swore to give Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob
but you will not cross into it
Gospels & Acts: He gave him no inheritance here, not even a foot of ground
But God promised to give possession of the land to Abraham and his descendants, even though he did not yet have a child
The letters: By faith he dwelt in the promised land as a stranger in a foreign country

rows.alike: Genesis repeats 'I will give this land to your offspring' to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; Exodus 33:1 and Deuteronomy 34:4 quote it, 'I will give it to your descendants'; Acts 7:5 reports it as 'God promised to give possession of the land to Abraham and his descendants'.
rows.different: Genesis 13:15 adds 'forever', and 17:8 and 48:4 'an eternal possession', 'an everlasting possession'. Acts 7:5 says God 'gave him no inheritance here, not even a foot of ground', and Hebrews 11:9 that he 'dwelt in the promised land as a stranger'. In Deuteronomy 34:4 Moses is shown the land and told 'you will not cross into it'.

rows.title: The fruit of your womb blessed

Genesis: by the Almighty who blesses you
with blessings of the breasts and womb
Psalms & elsewhere: He will bless the fruit of your womb and the produce of your land
Now if you faithfully obey the voice of the LORD your God
The fruit of your womb will be blessed, as well as the produce of your land
The LORD will make you prosper abundantly-in the fruit of your womb
the LORD your God will make you abound in all the work of your hands and in the fruit of your womb
The fruit of your womb will be cursed
Gospels & Acts: Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb!

rows.alike: Deuteronomy 28:4 and Luke 1:42 both call 'the fruit of your womb' blessed; Deuteronomy 7:13 has 'He will bless the fruit of your womb', and Genesis 49:25 'blessings of the breasts and womb'.
rows.different: In Deuteronomy 28 the blessing follows 'if you faithfully obey the voice of the LORD your God', and Deuteronomy 7:13 and 28:4 take in 'the produce of your land' as well; Deuteronomy 28:18 sets the same words under a curse. Luke 1:42 says it to one woman, 'Blessed are you among women'.

rows.title: The LORD bless you

The Prophets: May the LORD bless you, O righteous dwelling place, O holy mountain
Psalms & elsewhere: This is how you are to bless the Israelites
May the LORD bless you and keep you
So they shall put My name on the Israelites, and I will bless them
May the LORD bless you, my daughter
The LORD bless you, because you showed this kindness to Saul your lord
May you be blessed by the LORD, the Maker of heaven and earth
May the LORD bless you from Zion
May the LORD, the Maker of heaven and earth, bless you from Zion

rows.alike: Each asks a blessing from God on the one addressed: 'May the LORD bless you' (Numbers 6:24, Ruth 3:10, Psalm 128:5, Jeremiah 31:23), 'May God Almighty bless you' (Genesis 28:3).
rows.different: Numbers 6:24 is the form given for Aaron and his sons, 'This is how you are to bless the Israelites', and 6:27 adds 'they shall put My name on the Israelites, and I will bless them'. Psalms 128:5 and 134:3 add 'from Zion'; Jeremiah 31:23 addresses a place, 'O righteous dwelling place, O holy mountain'; in Ruth, 1 Samuel and 2 Samuel it passes between people as a greeting or a thanks.

rows.title: Cause His face to shine upon you and be gracious

Genesis: May God be gracious to you, my son
The Prophets: cause Your face to shine upon Your desolate sanctuary
Psalms & elsewhere: may the LORD cause His face to shine upon you and be gracious to you
Shine the light of Your face upon us, O LORD
Make Your face shine on Your servant
May God be gracious to us and bless us, and cause His face to shine upon us
Restore us, O God, and cause Your face to shine upon us, that we may be saved
Restore us, O God of Hosts, and cause Your face to shine upon us, that we may be saved
Restore us, O LORD God of Hosts; cause Your face to shine upon us, that we may be saved
Make Your face shine upon Your servant, and teach me Your statutes
oil that makes his face to shine

rows.alike: Numbers 6:25 and Psalm 67:1 share 'cause His face to shine upon' and 'be gracious'; the Psalms and Daniel 9:17 turn the words into a prayer, 'cause Your face to shine upon'.
rows.different: Numbers 6:25 speaks to 'you'; Psalm 67:1 prays 'upon us'; Psalm 80 adds 'that we may be saved', Psalm 119:135 'and teach me Your statutes', and Daniel 9:17 asks it for 'Your desolate sanctuary'. In Genesis 43:29 Joseph says 'May God be gracious to you, my son' to his brother. Psalm 104:15 uses 'his face to shine' of the effect of oil on a man.

rows.title: Give you peace

Psalms & elsewhere: may the LORD lift up His countenance toward you and give you peace
the LORD blesses His people with peace
Gospels & Acts: Peace I leave with you; My peace I give to you. I do not give to you as the world gives
The letters: Now may the Lord of peace Himself give you peace at all times and in every way

rows.alike: Numbers 6:26 and 2 Thessalonians 3:16 both put 'give you peace' as a wish, 'may the LORD ... give you peace', 'may the Lord of peace Himself give you peace'; Psalm 29:11 has 'blesses His people with peace' and John 14:27 'My peace I give to you'.
rows.different: Numbers 6:26 asks it of 'the LORD', 2 Thessalonians 3:16 of 'the Lord of peace Himself', adding 'at all times and in every way'. In John 14:27 Jesus speaks in the first person and adds 'I do not give to you as the world gives'.

rows.title: He lifted up his hands and blessed them

Psalms & elsewhere: Aaron lifted up his hands toward the people and blessed them
having made the sin offering, the burnt offering, and the peace offering, he stepped down
Gospels & Acts: He lifted up His hands and blessed them
While He was blessing them, He left them and was carried up into heaven

rows.alike: Both give a blessing with lifted hands: 'Aaron lifted up his hands toward the people and blessed them' (Leviticus 9:22), 'He lifted up His hands and blessed them' (Luke 24:50).
rows.different: Aaron blesses the people 'having made the sin offering, the burnt offering, and the peace offering', and then 'he stepped down'; in Luke 24:51 Jesus, 'While He was blessing them', 'left them and was carried up into heaven'.

rows.title: I am sending you

Genesis: Get ready; I am sending you to them
The Prophets: Whom shall I send? Who will go for Us?
to everyone I send you, you must go, and all that I command you, you must speak
I am sending you to the Israelites, to a rebellious nation

Psalms & elsewhere: Therefore, go! I am sending you to Pharaoh
Fill your horn with oil and go. I am sending you to Jesse of Bethlehem
the mission on which I am sending you
Gospels & Acts: Behold, I am sending you out like sheep among wolves

I am sending you to them
I am sending you prophets and wise men and teachers

rows.alike: God says 'I am sending you' to Moses (Exodus 3:10), Samuel (1 Samuel 16:1) and Ezekiel (Ezekiel 2:3), and Jesus says 'I am sending you' to the disciples (Matthew 10:16, Luke 10:3, John 20:21) and to Paul (Acts 26:17).
rows.different: Exodus 3:10, 1 Samuel 16:1 and Luke 10:3 add a command to go; in Isaiah 6:8 the prophet offers himself, 'Here am I. Send me!'; Jeremiah 1:7 and Ezekiel 2:4 add what is to be spoken. John 20:21 sets it beside 'As the Father has sent Me'; Matthew 10:16 and Luke 10:3 add 'among wolves'. In 1 Samuel 21:2 and 2 Chronicles 2:13 'I am sending you' is a man's errand, not a commission to speak for God.

rows.title: I am with you

Genesis: I will be with you and bless you
Do not be afraid, for I am with you
Look, I am with you, and I will watch over you wherever you go
The Prophets: Do not fear, for I am with you
Do not be afraid, for I am with you
Do not be afraid of them, for I am with you to deliver you
since I am with you to deliver you

For I am with you to save you
for I am with you to save you and deliver you from him
do not be afraid, declares the LORD, for I am with you
Work! For I am with you, declares the LORD of Hosts
Psalms & elsewhere: I will surely be with you

so they may know that I am with you just as I was with Moses
Gospels & Acts: And surely I am with you always, even to the end of the age

rows.alike: God says 'I am with you' to Isaac and Jacob (Genesis 26:24, 28:15), to Moses and Joshua (Exodus 3:12, Joshua 3:7) and through the prophets (Isaiah 41:10, Jeremiah 1:8, Haggai 1:13); Jesus says 'I am with you always' (Matthew 28:20), and the Lord says 'I am with you' to Paul (Acts 18:10).
rows.different: Many pair it with 'Do not be afraid' (Genesis 26:24, Joshua 1:9, Isaiah 43:5, Jeremiah 1:8). Genesis 28:15 and Joshua 1:9 add 'wherever you go'; Jeremiah adds 'to deliver you' and 'to save you'; Haggai 2:4 joins it to 'Work!'; Matthew 28:20 adds 'always, even to the end of the age'.

rows.title: To all nations, into all the world

The Prophets: I will send survivors from among them to the nations
